item.title: Curt Cignetti fires back at Indiana 'easy' schedule critics: 'I really don't give a s---'
item.description: Indiana coach Curt Cignetti slammed critics of the Hoosiers' soft schedule, saying the narrative fuels the 9-1 team's chip with CFP rankings looming.
item.content:encoded:
Indiana Hoosiers head football coach Curt Cignetti doesn’t want to hear a peep about their strength of schedule compared to other College Football Playoff hopefuls.

Cignetti, whose team is 9-1 and 6-1 in Big Ten play, has remained at No. 6 in the AP Top 25 poll for the past five weeks, and is sitting at No. 9 in the CFP rankings.

The CFP committee will unveil another week of rankings on Tuesday, but the eight teams above Indiana all picked up wins like they did on Saturday, so there might not be much movement.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Either way, Cignetti was asked by a student reporter, Ian Plaskoff, on Monday during his news conference about his team’s conference record, and furthermore, how those teams have fared after facing them. In total, Indiana’s conference opponents are a combined 8-16, and Plaskoff believed it was indicative of how physical the Hoosiers can be rather than what the discourse has been about their schedule.

It is believed by some that Indiana has benefited from a weaker schedule not just this season, but in years past. In the last three years since Cignetti took over the program, they are 36-3.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Cignetti had time today to bash all those with that thinking.

"Well, you know, we don’t play anybody. We have a soft schedule, right?" he said. "That’s all I’ve heard around here for three years. People like to discredit us and what we’ve accomplished. … The good thing about it is, I think it feeds into our motivation and our chip. And that’s why I’m not afraid to keep it alive. And you know what? I’m 65 years old and I really don’t give a s---."

Cignetti acknowledged that his comments were going to only fuel the fire surrounding the Hoosiers’ "easy" schedule, but he didn’t care.

He went on to point out how Northwestern and Nebraska were both undefeated before playing them earlier this season. Their only blemish on the record was against Ohio State, who lost Julian Sayin during the game and hasn’t seen him return since.

Cignetti called it a "layup" that they missed in terms of losing to the Buckeyes, but their conference rival losing back-to-back games after beating them is being viewed as Indiana not facing a quality opponent in Ohio State.

"We ripped the heart out of that team," Cignetti said. "They haven’t been the same since without the quarterback. … We missed a layup."

Cignetti admitted, "You get tired of the narrative sometimes," but these are the reigning national champions. Yes, they are without their Heisman-winning quarterback, Fernando Mendoza, and many other key pieces of that undefeated squad from a season ago.

But convincing wins against Washington this upcoming weekend, and Purdue during "Rivalry Week" to close out the regular season, could turn the dial down on the outside noise.

The Huskies are 6-4, but 3-4 in Big Ten play, this season as they host the Hoosiers on Saturday.

item.title: Hillary Clinton picks a foreign politician she believes is now the ‘leader of the free world’
item.description: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton argued Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney may be the current "leader of the free world" instead of President Donald Trump.
item.content:encoded:
Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton argued during an interview aired Sunday that if any politician qualifies as the current "leader of the free world," it would be Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney.

MS NOW host Rachel Maddow interviewed Clinton at the Temple Emanu-El Streicker Center in New York City and asked, "Do you think that there is a leader of the free world right now?"

"Maybe Mark Carney," Clinton said.

"That’s what I was going to ask," Maddow said. "He’s certainly articulating a vision of the free countries of the world and of — of the liberty-loving nations of the world that is about being stronger together."

CARNEY CASTS HIMSELF AS NATO DEFENDER AMID TRUMP BEEF, DESPITE CANADA MISSING KEY BENCHMARK FOR DECADES

The relationship between the United States and Canada has been strained following President Donald Trump's suggestions that Canada become the 51st U.S. state and his decision to impose tariffs on Canadian goods.

Clinton also argued that while some individual European leaders stood out, the continent as a whole was too disorganized. 

"And, you know, there are some good individual European leaders, but Europe has got to get itself organized so that, you know, the sum of the parts adds up to some kind of a whole and be able to do a better job at making some tough decisions, particularly with respect to Ukraine," she said. "They need to release the $250 million of Russian assets that are frozen in those Belgian banks and use it to defend Ukraine, just for starters."

"So if they can begin to make some collective decisions, then I think you’ll see other leaders emerge," Clinton continued. "But there’s going to be, as you know, Rachel, some very consequential elections in Europe this year, like the presidency of France. And if a populist pro-Putin party emerges with a leader who is very close to Putin and very beholden to Putin, Marine Le Pen, becomes the president of France, then we have new problems that we’re going to have to deal with."

TRUMP’S PROPOSED RUSSIA DEAL RAISES NATO ALARM AS EX-COMMANDER WARNS PUTIN SEEKS INFLUENCE OVER EUROPE

Earlier in the interview, Clinton argued that Trump had done "immeasurable damage" to America’s standing on the world stage with foreign policy that she described as "dangerous and incoherent.’

She also accused Trump of catering to "strongmen leaders."

"We are, unfortunately, seeing someone who admires strongmen leaders, thinks he is one, and believes in the old-fashioned concept of spheres of power," Clinton said. "And honestly, I don’t think it’s exaggerating to say that he’s perfectly fine with Putin doing whatever he wants with Ukraine and the rest of Europe." 

"He’s perfectly fine with Xi doing whatever he wants with Asia, as long as he can dominate the Western Hemisphere, and that all of them are some kind of triumvirate that is going to decide what the rest of us are capable of doing and what kind of society we will live under," she added. 

White House spokesman Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital, "President Trump is creating good-paying jobs, securing trillions of dollars in investments, and positioning our country to dominate the remainder of the 21st century. Meanwhile, Crooked Hillary Clinton is still whining about her spectacular 2016 election defeat. It’s time for Hillary to move on."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE OF MEDIA AND CULTURE

Morgan Murphy, a former White House official and former Pentagon press secretary, told Fox News Digital in response to Clinton's comments, "Canada's economy is chasing Mississippi's, and its armed forces couldn't scare the Salvation Army. It’s obvious Hillary still can’t admit the obvious: she lost [to] Trump, and he’s still the leader of the free world."

Theo Wold, a former White House deputy assistant for domestic policy under Trump, also criticized Clinton's comments.

"Canada’s PM Carney is nothing close to being the leader of the free world," Wold told Fox News Digital. "The Canadian economy is contracting; Canadian culture is at its weakest point as a consequence of mass immigration and proliferating crime and budget problems; separatist movements across the Canadian federation are gaining strength; and most of all, to the extent Canada projects power at all, it does so only from within the sphere of U.S. power projection and military might in the Western Hemisphere, making Canada at best a younger sibling piggybacking on America’s power projection around the world."

"Carney, pretending to be 2026’s Marshall Tito, used several high-profile speeches to criticize the America First movement and pitch a small state ‘non-aligned movement,’" he added. "There are no takers for this idiotic gambit outside of EU cultural elites in the dying capitals of Europe."

item.title: Fight reportedly breaks out between passengers aboard Chicago-bound flight, FBI responds
item.description: A passenger reportedly assaulted another traveler aboard Qatar Airways flight QR725 from Doha to Chicago, prompting an FBI and police response.
item.content:encoded:
An in-flight physical altercation reportedly broke out aboard a Chicago-bound Qatar Airways flight, prompting police and FBI agents to respond upon the aircraft’s arrival, according to officials.

Flight QR725, a Boeing 777, departed from Doha, Qatar, and landed at Chicago O’Hare International Airport in the afternoon, according to flight tracker AirNav radar.

Aviation outlet AirLive first reported the incident.

SHOCKING MID-FLIGHT BRAWL ERUPTS AFTER TAKEOFF, SENDING FLIGHT BACK TO AIRPORT

"The FBI and local law enforcement responded to an incident as described," the FBI Chicago office told Fox News.

Officials did not release any additional information regarding the circumstances of the assault.

FRONTIER PASSENGERS TACKLE MAN WHO ALLEGEDLY CHOKED OFF-DUTY FLIGHT ATTENDANT, TRIED TO OPEN DOOR MID-FLIGHT

According to cockpit communications, a passenger seated in row 32 physically assaulted another traveler seated in the row directly ahead, AirLive reported.

The outlet said the pilots noted in the recording that multiple passengers aboard the aircraft witnessed the altercation.

The flight crew contacted air traffic control shortly before landing to request that police meet the aircraft at the gate.

Fox News reached out to the Chicago Police Department, O’Hare International Airport, and Qatar Airways for more information.

item.title: Ecuador's president denies US operates military base despite reports of troop buildup
item.description: Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa denies the U.S. operates a military base at Taura Air Base, describing American personnel's activities as temporary.
item.content:encoded:
Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa denied that the United States operates a military base in his country after an Agence France-Presse (AFP) investigation signaled an expanded U.S. military presence at an air base near the port city of Guayaquil.

"Sometimes there's a specific mission. Sometimes there's a specific operation," Noboa told the news outlet Altavoz, describing U.S. personnel at Taura Air Base as carrying out "temporary activities" under a bilateral security agreement, including intelligence-gathering drone flights.

"We work together. It's not an American base. It's an Ecuadoran base," he commented.

THE UNLIKELY SOUTH AMERICAN ALLY HELPING LEAD TRUMP'S DRUG CARTEL CRACKDOWN

Noboa's remarks came about a month after AFP had documented an unusual deployment of U.S. military aircraft, dozens of tents and construction of new infrastructure at the air base.

The investigation identified approximately 20 U.S. military flights arriving at Taura between June and mid-October, along with internal documents confirming the presence of American troops.

Several flights originated from U.S. military installations, including Marine Corps Air Station Cherry Point in North Carolina and Dover Air Force Base in Delaware, with stopovers in Puerto Rico and Panama.

The buildup also raised legal concerns among senior Ecuadorian military officials.

AFP cited a September letter in which then-Air Force commander Gen. Mauricio Salazar asked military leaders to clarify the legality of the deployment. Salazar was subsequently removed from his post and reassigned to a less senior role, the report said.

The increased U.S. military presence comes after Ecuadorian voters rejected a Noboa-backed referendum in November 2025 that would have amended the country's constitution to lift its ban on foreign military bases.

US MILITARY BOARDS, SEARCHES AND SINKS VESSEL ALLEGEDLY SUPPORTING LOS CHONEROS NARCO-TERRORISTS

Despite the referendum's defeat, Quito and Washington have deepened security cooperation to combat drug trafficking and transnational organized crime.

Human Rights Watch has described the United States as Ecuador's primary security partner in its crackdown on organized crime, providing equipment, training, intelligence and direct military support.

The watchdog characterized the partnership as "perilous," warning that "both governments have engaged in serious human rights violations fuelled by their insistence on framing their confrontations with organised crime groups as a kind of war."

Since returning to the White House in January 2025, President Donald Trump has designated several Latin American cartels as foreign terrorist organizations and authorized military strikes against vessels in international waters suspected of drug trafficking.

WHITE HOUSE HIGHLIGHTS 'STEEPEST' EVER DECLINE IN US CASUALTIES FROM CARTELS AMID BOAT STRIKES

Ecuador has also emerged as a key ally in Trump's crackdown on drug cartels and narcoterrorism, with U.S. and Ecuadorian forces working together to intercept narcotics shipments and dismantle transnational criminal networks, the country's foreign minister told Fox News Digital in September.

 Roberto Kury said closer cooperation with Washington had delivered "a lot of positive results" in recent months, citing drug shipments intercepted through U.S. intelligence and joint operations.

"There is an intelligence (sic) and cooperation from the United States, but there is also always the presence of Ecuadorian military or police. They work together," Kury told Fox News Digital on the sidelines of the U.N. General Assembly.

"Most of the drugs go to the United States. So that’s why the United States shares the problem," Kury said.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio has also praised Ecuador as the United States' most "aggressive" partner in its Western Hemisphere crackdown.

Fox News Digital has reached out to Southcom for comment.

item.title: Trump admin opens civil rights probes into 15 colleges over DEI grants
item.description: The Education Department's Office for Civil Rights opened probes into CUNY's NYC Men Teach program over alleged race- and sex-based discrimination.
item.content:encoded:
The U.S. Department of Education announced Monday that it has opened federal civil rights investigations into several teacher preparation programs following complaints alleging race and sex-based discrimination.

According to a department press release, the Office for Civil Rights (OCR) formally opened the probes on Friday, Nov. 13, targeting programs "designed to recruit, retain, and support future educators" that allegedly "provide sex or race-specific recruitment, support, and financial opportunities for candidates in violation of civil rights laws."

The initial four entities under investigation are the City University of New York (CUNY), the University of Maryland College of Education, the Minnesota Department of Education, and the Minnesota Office of Higher Education. The department noted that OCR is also opening investigations into 11 additional universities over similar allegations.

DEPT OF ED PUSHES AHEAD WITH EFFORTS TO DISMANTLE FEDERAL BUREAUCRACY AFTER BLUE WAVE

The department said OCR will examine whether the programs violate Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, which prohibits discrimination based on race, color or national origin, or Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972, which prohibits sex-based discrimination in federally funded education programs.

Specifically, federal investigators are examining:

* City University of New York (CUNY): Under investigation over its NYC Men Teach program for alleged discrimination on the basis of both race and sex.

* University of Maryland: Under investigation for alleged racial discrimination in its administration of the Maryland Higher Education Commission Teacher Quality and Diversity Grant Program and the EdTerps CARES Network.

* Minnesota Department of Education: Under investigation for alleged racial discrimination through its Education Tuition Assistance Program, which provides scholarships and stipends to students in teacher preparation programs.

* Minnesota Office of Higher Education: Under investigation for alleged racial discrimination in its administration of the Minnesota Aspiring Teachers of Color Scholarship Pilot Program and the Underrepresented Student Teacher Grant.

A NEW YORK UNIVERSITY FACES JUSTICE DEPARTMENT INVESTIGATION OVER 'BLACK MALE INITIATIVE'

A spokesperson from the Minnesota Office of Higher Education told Fox News Digital: "The Minnesota Underrepresented Student Teacher Grant (USTG) was established by the Minnesota Legislature in 2021. OHE is implementing this program in accordance with State law," 

"The Minnesota Aspiring Teachers of Color Scholarship was a pilot program also established by the Minnesota Legislature in 2021. This scholarship is no longer available to Minnesotans as funding ended after the 2024-25 academic year," the spokesperson added.

The investigations stem from complaints filed by the Equal Protection Project (EPP), a legal advocacy group founded by Cornell Law School professor William Jacobson as part of the Legal Insurrection Foundation.

"The Equal Protection Project welcomes the U.S. Department of Education's Office for Civil Rights' decision to open investigations into complaints alleging violations of Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964," Jacobson told Fox News Digital, adding that his organization will cooperate fully with the investigations. 

"The opening of these investigations reflects OCR's determination that the allegations warrant further review and underscores the importance of ensuring that all students have access to educational environments free from discrimination based on race, color, or national origin," Jacobson added.

MINNESOTA YANKS RACE-BASED GRANT AFTER DOJ INITIATED CIVIL RIGHTS REVIEW, DOJ REVEALS

EPP chief counsel Maureen S. Riordan echoed that sentiment, calling the decision "an important step toward addressing serious concerns regarding compliance with federal civil rights protections and ensuring that educational institutions uphold their obligations under Title VI."

A Department of Education spokesperson told Fox News Digital, "The Department will open investigations across the nation based on credible reports that universities with education programs withhold opportunities for recruitment and financial support from candidates based solely on race," adding, "Teachers are the heartbeat of our schools, and the Trump Administration will ensure a future where students are [judged] based on their merit and grit, not the color of their skin."

The enforcement push aligns with President Donald Trump’s effort to eliminate diversity, equity, and inclusion (DEI) initiatives since he returned to office in January 2025. Shortly after his inauguration, Trump signed executive orders aimed at ending DEI programs across the federal workforce and federal contracting, directing agencies to enforce civil rights laws in alignment with the Supreme Court’s 2023 Students for Fair Admissions v. Harvard ruling, which struck down race-based affirmative action in college admissions.

TRUMP ADMINISTRATION PROPOSES STRIPPING TAX-EXEMPT STATUS FROM SCHOOLS USING RACE-BASED PROGRAMS

Department officials previously told Fox News Digital that the administration, led by Education Secretary Linda McMahon, plans to intensify efforts to dismantle federal bureaucracy, strengthen parental rights, and enforce federal civil rights laws against higher education institutions following Democratic victories in key midterm elections earlier this month.

A CUNY spokesperson told Fox News Digital: "CUNY is proud of its role educating the teachers of tomorrow and our programs are open to all students regardless of race, gender or national origin." 

The University of Maryland declined to comment. The Minnesota Department of Education did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Netflix's 'Untold' series tackles the New York Giants' miracle Super Bowl XLII upset of the Patriots next
item.description: Netflix's "Untold: One Giant Upset" lands Dec. 21, featuring Eli Manning, Michael Strahan, and Tom Brady on the Giants' shocking Super Bowl XLII win.
item.content:encoded:
Christmas came early for Giants fans. It's not Jaxson Dart's return, though all of New Jersey is eagerly waiting for that day.

Netflix announced on Monday that a new installment in the Untold series will drop Dec. 21. Titled One Giant Upset, the documentary focuses on the miracle New York Giants team that upset the Patriots in 2008.

THE CRAIG CARTON SHOW–UNFILTERED, UNAPOLOGETIC AND UNMISSABLE. DOWNLOAD HIS DAILY PODCAST NOW!

Netflix's Untold has previously unpacked the wildest sagas in sports, from Manti Te'o's catfishing scandal and the Malice at the Palace brawl to Johnny Manziel and Urban Meyer's Florida Gators. Now, Big Blue gets the spotlight.

ELI MANNING FINALLY REVEALS WHY HE WRIGGLED HIS WAY OUT OF PLAYING FOR CHARGERS

Are they going to retell stories we've all heard in the nearly two decades since the G-Men won that ring? Of course. Will it be sweet to revisit the night Eli Manning and company broke New England's team of destiny? Absolutely.

For Giants fans, that 2007 squad remains unforgettable because of how ugly things started. New York opened 0-2 with head coach Tom Coughlin on the hot seat before rattling off 11 straight road wins, including playoff upsets in Tampa, Dallas, and minus-one-degree Green Bay.

SUPER BOWL CHAMPION PLAXICO BURRESS COMPARES PLAYING FOR JETS TO HIS TIME IN PRISON: 'A F—KING LOSER'

After trading haymakers with New England in a 38-35 Week 17 loss, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo unleashed his four-end NASCAR pass rush in the rematch: Super Bowl XLII. Michael Strahan, Justin Tuck, and Osi Umenyiora sacked Tom Brady five times, holding the historic offense to 14 points.

Then came the legendary fourth quarter: Manning slipping out of three jerseys, David Tyree pinning the football to his helmet, and Plaxico Burress — playing on a torn ankle ligament — hauling in the winning score.

TOM BRADY ADMITS TO MORE MOTIVATION AFTER DEFLATEGATE SUSPENSION, REVEALS WHAT HE DID WHILE AWAY FROM PATRIOTS

Manning and Strahan lead the documentary's Giants lineup alongside Coughlin, Spagnuolo, Tuck, Shaun O'Hara, Antonio Pierce, Sam Madison, Burress, and Tyree, joined by Brady.

Hearing Brady get honest about the toughest loss of his career adds real juice to the show. Still, watching Netflix celebrate one of the landmark games in NFL history highlights a total joke.

DREW BREES GIVES HIS STANCE ON ELI MANNING'S PRO FOOTBALL HALL OF FAME CANDIDACY AMID STRONG DEBATE

Super Bowl XLII defined an era, and Manning owns two Super Bowl MVPs against the Belichick-Brady dynasty, yet the Pro Football Hall of Fame has passed him over twice. Make it make sense. Leaving the architect of football's biggest upset out of Canton is a Giant mistake.

item.title: Democratic judge under fire for releasing violent offenders calls bail law a ‘direct assault’ on rights
item.description: Judge David Carpenter called Alabama’s Aniah’s Law a ‘direct assault’ on constitutional rights, citing defendants’ presumption of innocence.
item.content:encoded:
A Democratic Alabama judge facing mounting scrutiny over past decisions to release violent offenders is criticizing a state law that allows defendants charged with certain violent crimes to be denied bail.

Circuit Court Judge David Carpenter called Alabama’s Aniah’s Law a direct assault on constitutional rights, arguing that defendants should not be held indefinitely based solely on criminal charges, citing the constitutional presumption of innocence.

In a social media post, Carpenter argued that critics of government overreach involving license plate cameras, such as Flock cameras, are not equally concerned about expanded pretrial detention laws.

"Can someone explain to me why the people who are so alarmed that a flock camera might spot their car on a public road, and they call that government overreach, are silent on the fact that voters across the country keep overwhelmingly passing new laws to empower the government to hold you in jail indefinitely on the basis of a charge only," Carpenter said.

THE SURVEILLANCE CAMERA ON YOUR STREET CORNER: LAWFUL SPYING OR CONSTITUTIONALLY PROBLEMATIC?

"These laws, like Alabama’s Aniah’s Law, are a direct assault on the Constitutional guarantee of the presumption of innocence. But no one is talking about this at all, much less expressing the hysteria associated with having a camera see a license plate," he said.

Although Aniah’s Law was originally passed in 2022, Alabama voters approved a major constitutional amendment this year expanding the law to cover additional offenses. The expansion added attempted murder, solicitation or conspiracy to commit murder, and discharging a firearm or explosives into an occupied dwelling, building or vehicle.

"We are all one accusation away from being a criminal defendant," Carpenter said in a post on Facebook.

WHITE HOUSE CALLS DC POLICIES 'INSANITY' AFTER 19-YEAR-OLD GUNMAN GETS PROBATION IN SHOOTING

Carpenter has faced controversy over several judicial decisions over the years. Local outlet 1819 News reported that he previously described himself online as a "far left, liberal, progressive, democratic socialist."

In April 2023, Carpenter approved a plea deal for Damien McDaniel, who was arrested in 2019 for shooting two people in a car when he was 17 years old, 1819 News reported. After being released from jail, McDaniel allegedly went on a 14-month shooting spree across Alabama, killing 18 people and injuring more than 30 others.

Carpenter also granted bond to Raukeem Cunningham in connection with the 2022 shooting death of a teenage girl, the outlet reported. While out on bond, Cunningham was arrested and charged with fatally shooting three people at a Bessemer gas station in 2024, prompting the revocation of his original bond.

In addition, Carpenter reportedly dismissed a 2015 rape charge against Fredrick Terrenda Hampton in 2019, according to reports. The dismissal came just two days before Hampton met Paighton Houston, who later disappeared. Her body was found buried behind a home after she died of an accidental overdose.

CONVICTED SERIAL RAPIST ORIGINALLY SENTENCED TO 124 YEARS WALKS FREE AFTER 20, SPARKING OUTRAGE

Hampton pleaded guilty to abuse of a corpse in connection with Houston’s death, and Carpenter gave him a 20-year split sentence with only three years to serve in custody, the outlet said.

Houston’s mother ultimately asked Alabama Attorney General Steve Marshall to investigate Carpenter over his decision to release Hampton, whom critics described as a repeat sex offender.

During his campaign for judicial office, Carpenter said one of his major goals was to "reform the criminal justice system in Alabama."

"If elected, I will work to reduce the number of repeat offenders while addressing the expensive problem of prison overcrowding in Alabama," he said.

item.title: James Comer launches bid for Kentucky governor
item.description: House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., is launching a campaign for Kentucky governor Monday night, a source familiar with the plan says.
item.content:encoded:
House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer, R-Ky., is launching a campaign for governor on Monday night.

"Serving this state is a calling for me," Comer said during a tele-townhall. "Kentucky needs a leader whose policies will lead to growth and good-paying jobs. We need a leader whose priority will be to reduce taxes so Kentuckians can keep more of what they earn."

Comer teased a "major announcement" for Monday night earlier in the day. A source familiar with his plans told Fox News Digital it would be his long-awaited campaign to lead the commonwealth of Kentucky.

REDISTRICTING EFFORTS BLOW UP IN REPUBLICANS' FACES AMID HISTORIC HOUSE LOSSES

Comer spent the majority of his announcement fielding questions from Kentuckians on topics like education, small business, and high prices.

Among the policies he advocated for was reducing Kentucky's income tax to zero.

"We all talk about attracting new businesses and new industry to Kentucky," Comer said. "If we can get that existing income tax to zero, people are going to have more money to spend, and we're going to be able to attract more good-paying jobs to Kentucky, which will be able to keep our best and brightest in the state and help our state grow into the future."

Kentucky's gubernatorial election will take place in November 2027, with the primaries set for May of that year.

Gov. Andy Beshear, who is widely considered a potential contender for the Democratic presidential primary in 2028, is term-limited.

Comer ran for Kentucky governor in 2015 but narrowly lost the GOP primary to former Gov. Matt Bevin.

But this election cycle will likely see the House lawmaker enter as the frontrunner for his party's nomination.

Comer has served in the House of Representatives since November 2016, when he won a special election for Kentucky's 1st congressional district. Since then, his profile has skyrocketed as the top Republican on the House Oversight Committee for the better part of the last six years.

FOX NEWS VOTER POLL: HOW DEMOCRATS TOOK CONTROL OF THE SENATE

As committee chairman since Republicans took back the House majority in 2023, he's launched investigations into former President Joe Biden's use of autopen and the federal government's handling of Jeffrey Epstein's case, among others.

And despite Beshear's popularity as the state's two-term Democratic governor, Kentucky has historically been seen as a red state.

President Donald Trump defeated former Vice President Kamala Harris by roughly 30 points there in 2024. He beat former President Joe Biden there by 25.9% in 2020.

item.title: Illegal alien accused of attempted murder at large after Rikers release despite ICE detainer: DHS
item.description: Delon Raymond Jaundoo, a Guyanese citizen in the United States illegally, was freed from Rikers Island despite an ICE detainer, according to DHS.
item.content:encoded:
A Guyanese citizen living in the United States illegally remains at large after being released from custody in New York City earlier this month, despite facing multiple violent felony charges and an active federal immigration detainer, according to the Department of Homeland Security (DHS).

DHS officials stated that Delon Raymond Jaundoo was arrested in Brooklyn on charges including attempted murder, first- and second-degree assault, criminal use of a firearm, and multiple counts of criminal possession of a loaded weapon.

His prior criminal record also includes an arrest for third-degree assault.

U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) lodged an immigration detainer for Jaundoo on April 29, which the New York City Department of Correction declined to honor, allowing him to be released from Rikers Island.

MANHUNT UNDERWAY FOR VIOLENT ILLEGAL IMMIGRANT WHO WAS RELEASED UNDER NYC SANCTUARY POLICIES

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin criticized New York’s sanctuary policies following the release, arguing that state and local laws prevent cooperation with federal immigration authorities even in cases involving violent offenses.

Jaundoo lawfully entered the country during the Obama administration but overstayed his authorized stay, which expired in January 2015, according to DHS.

"Despite these violent charges, sanctuary politicians in New York refused to honor ICE’s detainer and released this criminal back onto the streets to put more American lives in danger," Mullin said in a statement. "Under Governor Kathy Hochul, New York has become a hotbed of illegal alien crime."

DHS SECRETARY BASHES NEW YORK LEADERSHIP AFTER ANNOUNCING THOUSANDS OF ARRESTS IN SWEEPING OPERATION

"The sooner we put an end to these reckless sanctuary policies, the sooner we can all work together to make America safe again," he added.

Jaundoo's release comes amid ongoing restrictions on local cooperation with federal immigration enforcement.

HOCHUL BOASTS 'I JUST BANNED IT' AS NEW YORK OUTLAWS LOCAL POLICE PARTNERSHIPS WITH ICE

Upon taking office, New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani signed an executive order limiting city coordination with ICE, and a state law signed by Gov. Kathy Hochul took effect in August barring local authorities from cooperating with federal immigration officials.

DHS stated that several other illegal immigrants arrested for or convicted of violent crimes, including murder, arson, assault, and rape, have similarly been released from custody under the state's current policies.

"Governor Hochul has been clear: New York State is not and never will be a sanctuary for violent criminals," a spokesperson for Hochul told Fox News Digital. "By law, New York State always notifies federal immigration enforcement of any non-citizen serving a State prison sentence. Any assertion otherwise is a blatant mischaracterization of the facts meant to distract from the cruelty and violence we’ve seen from Secretary Mullin’s ICE agents."

Fox News Digital has reached out to Mamdani's office for comment.

item.title: Buster Posey headlines 27 names on the 2027 Major League Baseball Hall of Fame ballot
item.description: Buster Posey headlined the 14 first-timers on Major League Baseball's 2027 Hall of Fame ballot, eyeing first-ballot status after three World Series titles.
item.content:encoded:
Major League Baseball may be looking ahead to some contentious negotiations as the collective bargaining agreement is set to expire in a couple of weeks, but the National Baseball Hall of Fame voting process will not be hindered.

MLB revealed the 27 players that have made their way to the 2027 Hall of Fame ballot on Monday.

Among the field are 14 first-timers, and one in particular many believe should be heading into Cooperstown as a first-ballot Hall of Famer.

CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE

Buster Posey, the San Francisco Giants catching great who currently serves as the franchise’s president of baseball operations, has the chance to make it in on his first try, and the resumé backs it up.

Posey was the 2010 NL Rookie of the Year, the 2012 NL MVP, and helped lead the Giants to three World Series victories during his five years with the franchise. Posey played just 12 seasons in the league, but he tallied seven All-Star bids, five Silver Slugger Awards and owned a career WAR of 45, which sits 12th all time in franchise history, according to Baseball Reference.

item.title: Trump’s Asia trip takes Alaska detour as weather forces refueling stop change
item.description: Air Force One diverted its Alaska refueling stop from Anchorage to Fairbanks due to extreme weather as President Donald Trump's Asia trip heads to Manila.
item.content:encoded:
President Donald Trump’s flight to Asia took a detour Monday as extreme weather forced Air Force One to change its Alaska refueling stop before continuing to the Philippines.

Air Force One switched from Anchorage to Fairbanks to refuel under better weather conditions, a White House official confirmed to Fox News. The aircraft has since departed for Manila.

The president landed in Alaska at 4:28 p.m. ET for what was expected to be a roughly 90-minute refueling stop, according to the traveling White House press pool.

Reporters were not expected to see Trump during the stop, with their next anticipated appearance with the president upon his arrival in Manila.

TRUMP BRINGS TWO DIVIDED CABINET HEAVYWEIGHTS TO CHINA AS CONTROVERSY HANGS OVER HIGH-STAKES TALKS

Trump’s four-day Asia trip includes stops in the Philippines and China, regional economic and security summits and high-stakes meetings with world leaders.

Trump is expected to hold talks with Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin, and potentially North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.

The trip comes amid scrutiny of China’s access to advanced American artificial intelligence chips and competing views within Trump’s Cabinet over how to respond.

TRUMP LEAVES DOOR OPEN TO KIM JONG UN JOINING HIGH-STAKES TALKS WITH XI, PUTIN

Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are accompanying Trump following reports of a disagreement over whether to place Singapore-based Megaspeed on a U.S. trade blacklist. The company has faced allegations that its operations helped Chinese companies access restricted Nvidia chips. Megaspeed has denied wrongdoing.

Trump acknowledged the officials’ differing positions Monday, suggesting Lutnick may have delayed action to avoid escalating tensions with Beijing.

TWO TOP TRUMP CABINET OFFICIALS GO TO WAR OVER CHINA SPY SCANDAL AMID EXPLOSIVE ACCUSATIONS: REPORT

"We’re having a very good relationship with China right now, and I understand both sides of it, and I’ll make a decision," Trump said.

Trump also said he was not considering replacing Lutnick, telling reporters the commerce secretary has "done a very good job."

Fox News Digital's Ashley DiMella contributed to this report.

item.title: Follow the Leader: Democrats face party battle as divisions deepen
item.description: Democrats face internal divisions as Hakeem Jeffries and Chuck Schumer encounter resistance from members questioning their leadership and the party's direction.
item.content:encoded:
You can’t play follow the leader until you decide who you want to follow.

That’s the conundrum facing House and Senate Democrats. Not all House Democrats are on board with promoting House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries (D-N.Y.) to Speaker. And Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Md.) is challenging Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer (D-N.Y.) for Majority Leader.

"As of today, my position is no because that's what my constituents and my community is saying," said Rep.-elect Angela Gonzales-Torres (D-Calif.) when asked if she backed Jeffries, "It's really about the process. We want a democratic process. And that's what we're really fighting for. It's not about one person."

It may not be about one person. But no one is running against Jeffries. That’s why some Jeffries loyalists believe that House Democrats should endorse him for the Speakership by acclimation on Wednesday.

SENATE DEM CHALLENGING SEN CHUCK SCHUMER FOR LEADERSHIP POST BACKS HAKEEM JEFFRIES FOR HOUSE SPEAKER

Rep.-elect Jessica Killin (D-Colo.) flipped a district from red to blue and endorses Jeffries.

"He hasn't had the opportunity to work in the majority as a leader of our party yet and I want to give him that opportunity," said Killin.

Yet nearby in in the Centennial State, progressive Rep.-elect Melat Kiros (D-Colo.) isn’t in Jeffries camp.

"Not yet," said Kiros when asked by yours truly if she would vote for Jeffries. "Ultimately this is about making sure that there is a democratic process in lieu of there not being multiple candidates."

But reservations about Jeffries aren’t just coming from the left. Try the center. Rep.-elect Sam Forstag (D-MT) won a district in western Montana which President Trump carried by 11 points two years ago. Forstag.

"I haven't committed my vote to anybody," said Forstag. "I'll be voting for whoever's going to actually help us modernize the way this place works." 

HAKEEM JEFFRIES FACES PROGRESSIVE HOLDOUTS BUT NO RIVAL AS HOUSE SPEAKER RACE TAKES SHAPE

Before voters elected her to Congress, Killin toiled for multiple House Democrats as a chief of staff. She understands what Members must synthesize before supporting someone for leadership. 

"We have a wild and unwieldy freshman class. It's over 100 people. This is part of process," said Killin. "Each person needs to follow their own process on how we're electing leadership." 

House Republicans settled their leadership team last week, tapping Rep. Jim Jordan (R-Ohio) to serve as Minority Leader next year over current House Majority Leader Steve Scalise (R-La.). Rep.-elect Chris Stigall (R-Mo.) may consider investing in tubs of popcorn as he watches leadership machinations across the aisle. 

"They're going to have one heck of a fight on their hands deciding who the voice of their party going forward is going to be," predicted Stigall. "If Team Jeffries can somehow manage to wrangle and herd those cats, it'll be a miracle, frankly." 

In the Senate, Van Hollen says midterm wins by Democrats in states which haven’t been in the Democratic column in years spurred his candidacy for Majority Leader.

"We understand that this will be a competition," said Van Hollen. "I think it's important to give Senate Democrats a choice. That's what we just gave voters all over the country. A choice. They chose change."

Schumer has led Senate Democrats for a decade. Van Hollen is nearly nine years younger than the 75-year-old Schumer — who turns 76 next week. Van Hollen has at least five senators or senators-elect who caucus with the Democrats who will support him. There are three senators who associate with the Democrats who won’t back Schumer as the next Majority Leader. 

"I've been open that I'm not voting for Sen. Schumer," said Sen. Elissa Slotkin (D-Mich.). 

The revolt over Jeffries and Schumer reveals fractures between moderates and progressives. Plus old and new. Even Schumer’s hometown mayor sidestepped an opportunity to endorse the Brooklyn Democrat.

"I care less about who it is and I care more about what they do with that power," said New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani (D). 

That says, Schumer has vocal supporters — including an ally from the Empire State. 

"This caucus is grateful for the hard work of Sen. Schumer. No one has put in the time and effort that anyone has put into this cycle than he did," said Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand (D-N.Y.). "That is why you will see, despite all the grumblings, enormous gratitude for the hard work he has done to get us to this position." 

"Chris Van Hollen is a great colleague," said Sen. Richard Blumenthal (D-Conn.). "But I'm supporting Chuck Schumer." 

But even one Democrat aligned with Schumer says what gets done outweighs who does it. 

"I think no matter who is Leader, we're going to deliver on this agenda," said Sen. Ruben Gallego (D-Ariz.).

A small group of demonstrators cursed at Jeffries when he spoke at a Democrats’ conference in Colorado late last week. The protesters hollered about impeachment and called him a "f****** liar." Frication like that threatens to sidetrack Democrats. 

"There’s really a fight for the soul of the Democratic Party. Are they going to embrace these radical ideas?" asked Sen. Dave McCormick (R-Pa.) on Fox. 

Some incoming progressives contend there’s no internal strife. 

"People try to say we're we're fractured as a party. In reality, we're all working on the same message," said Rep.-elect Donavan McKinney (D-Mich.).

RACHEL MADDOW WELCOMES 'BIG FIGHT' BETWEEN SOCIALIST AND MODERATE DEMOCRATS AFTER MIDTERM WINS

One Democrat said the internecine arguments are natural at this stage with Democrats just capturing big majorities.

"I think a little bit of scrumming around inside the party is a good thing," said Rep.-elect Fred Wellman (D-Mo.) who defeated Rep. Ann Wagner (R-MO) in what had been an historically red district. "The wonderful thing about my party is we're more than happy to duke it out." 

Rep.-elect Eric Jones (D-Calif.) quibbles with the terminology characterizing Democratic disagreements.

"I wouldn't go so far as to say ‘duke it out’ because those are fighting words," said Jones. "But there are definitely open conversations. They're pretty collegial. Pretty collaborative."

But real differences exist. Sen. John Fetterman (D-Pa.) says he opposes what he termed Van Hollen’s "strong, anti-Israel kinds of views." 

"I can't really think of what Van Hollen is known for. But he became like a progressive darling. But I don't see that he has a path to be leader," said Fetterman on Fox.  

Liberal Democrats believe Van Hollen is willing to enact progressive priorities – which may be controversial among centrist Democrats.

"Sen. Van Hollen has been a long-time supporter of DC and DC statehood," said Washington, DC’s new non-voting delegate to the House, Del.-elect Robert White (D-DC). "I would get rid of the filibuster in order to get DC statehood."

On Fox, Van Hollen said he wouldn’t end the filibuster "right out of the gate." But the Maryland Democrat added that the filibuster was an "undemocratic provision."

Specifics matter in politics. They’ll matter if there’s a move to change the filibuster. Obliterating the filibuster might excite some progressives. But other Democrats may recoil. The same with Medicare for all. Progressives may embrace such a vote. But moderate Democrats who flipped red districts could abhor that prospect.

Those are the things which Democratic leaders must figure out. And when they do, only then will we know who is willing to follow them.

item.title: 'Bridgerton' star boycotts upcoming 'Harry Potter' TV show over author JK Rowling's transgender views
item.description: Actress Nicola Coughlan, a vocal supporter of transgender rights, said she'd never join HBO Max's "Harry Potter" series despite loving the original books.
item.content:encoded:
"Bridgerton" actress Nicola Coughlan declared Thursday she would never watch or appear in Warner Bros. Discovery and HBO Max's upcoming "Harry Potter" series because of author J.K. Rowling's views on transgender issues.

In an interview with The Observer, Coughlan spoke about her political activism, including fundraising for Palestinian causes, marching for abortion rights and advocating for transgender rights. Coughlan said she would not watch or participate in the upcoming adaptation of Rowling's fantasy series, despite her love for the original books. The show is scheduled to premiere Dec. 25.

"I will not be watching the new ‘Harry Potter’ show and I would never be in it," Coughlan said. "Look, I know people that are involved in those shows, and they're nice people and whatever, but it's not for me."

HBO’S 'HARRY POTTER' GETS A HARD NO FROM 'BLACK MIRROR,' 'LOKI' DIRECTORS OVER JK ROWLING’S TRANS VIEWS

Rowling has defended women-only spaces and opposed some transgender rights policies. She also previously criticized Coughlan.

In 2025, Coughlan criticized Rowling for celebrating a unanimous ruling by the U.K. Supreme Court that the terms "woman" and "sex" in the Equality Act 2010 refer to biological sex. The ruling addressed the interpretation of the law, including provisions governing single-sex spaces.

Coughlan wrote on Instagram, "Keep your new ‘Harry Potter’ lads. Wouldn’t touch it with a 10-foot pole."

JK ROWLING REFUSES TO BACK DOWN IN ESSAY CALLING TRANS ACTIVISM 'ELITIST TO ITS CORE'

Following Coughlan's remarks, Rowling wrote on X that she did not know who Coughlan or actor Pedro Pascal was. Both actors had criticized Rowling.

In her interview with The Observer, Coughlan responded to Rowling's comments.

"Me, I could believe," Coughlan said. "But Pedro Pascal? You know who Pedro Pascal is, girl. Like, please."

Fox News Digital reached out to Warner Bros. Discovery and Rowling for comment but did not immediately receive a response.

ROYAL FAMILY FACES BACKLASH FROM CRITICS AFTER QUEEN CAMILLA HOSTS J.K. ROWLING

Christian Toto, host of the "Hollywood in Toto" podcast, told Fox News Digital that Coughlan's comments likely "won't move the needle a millimeter" on the upcoming series, which he described as one of the most hotly anticipated shows in a while.

"This is the easiest and laziest virtue signal possible for a less than recognizable actress. It's just one of many positions Hollywood is supposed to endorse," Toto told Fox News Digital. "End ICE. Trump is a dictator. J.K. Rowling is wrong on trans issues but they can't explain why. There's nothing brave or unexpected in Coughlan's comments. It's almost like she's reading from a script."

item.title: French troops secretly deployed inside Ukraine as ex-NATO chief praises Macron's 'guts'
item.description: President Emmanuel Macron's France reportedly runs covert "Volia" mission training Ukrainian troops as Zelenskyy holds fresh peace talks with the US.
item.content:encoded:
French troops have reportedly been operating secretly inside Ukraine for months, training Ukrainian forces and maintaining military equipment and, as NATO experts claim, President Emmanuel Macron is taking a more assertive role in supporting Kyiv against Russia.

The covert mission, codenamed "Volia," has operated since at least summer 2026, with small teams of French military personnel deployed on short-term assignments under the supervision of a French general, Radio France Internationale (RFI) reported Monday.

Agence France-Presse (AFP) also separately reported the French military presence, citing sources who said the troops were not involved in combat.

UKRAINE HITS PUTIN'S PRIZED BRIDGE IN RECORD DRONE BLITZ AS KREMLIN TELLS LAWMAKERS TO PREPARE FOR 'VICTORY'

The reports come as the United States and European allies pursue renewed, high-stakes negotiations to end Russia's war in Ukraine, raising questions about the extent of Western military involvement in the conflict.

Former NATO Supreme Allied Commander Europe Gen. Philip Breedlove meanwhile, told Fox News Digital that the covert French mission sends a powerful message to Russian President Vladimir Putin at a critical juncture for Europe.

"The timing of what the French are doing and their announcement of what they're doing is important," Breedlove said.

"A very powerful NATO ally — both politically and militarily — is making a strong statement of support for Ukraine.

"And this is what Mr. Putin needs to see. He needs to look across the line and see that the Western alliances, NATO in this case, are standing up for Ukraine."

"It's very important to remember that if Mr. Putin stops fighting, this war ends. If Ukraine stops fighting, Ukraine ends," he said before adding that this is "an existential war that we in the West need to support to the appropriate conclusion."

UKRAINE'S ATTACKS ON RUSSIA ARE PUSHING PUTIN CLOSER TO NEGOTIATING TABLE, TRUMP NATO AMBASSADOR SAYS

The French mission reportedly focuses on training Ukrainian troops and maintaining French-supplied equipment, including CAESAR self-propelled howitzers, Mirage 2000 fighter jets and precision-guided missiles.

French personnel have rotated between France, Poland and Ukraine under what RFI described as a "light and flexible" operational structure.

French newspaper Le Monde separately reported Monday that personnel had also worked alongside Ukrainian intelligence units on observation missions closer to the front lines.

The deployment would mark a significant step in Macron's military support for Kyiv despite repeated Russian warnings against Western troop involvement.

"I cannot imagine the French military would deploy into Ukraine without their commander-in-chief approving it," Breedlove said of Macron while noting that Western military training missions inside Ukraine predate Russia's full-scale invasion in February 2022.

"It's not new to have training facilities inside of Ukraine. But almost all of them, and almost everyone, left Ukraine when the war started, which I disagree with, but that was the decision," he said.

Breedlove also pointed to the Yavoriv military training facility in western Ukraine, where NATO countries helped train Ukrainian forces following Russia's initial intervention in 2014.

"In 2014, we had a training area called Yavoriv," he said.

"We had a large facility of NATO training ability there, and we trained Ukrainians all the time. When the war started back in 2014 — remembering this is a 12-year-long war — most of those nations left, to include the United States."

RIOT-TORN FRANCE STRUGGLES WITH CHAOS AT HOME AS MACRON EYES MILITARY MISSION THOUSANDS OF MILES AWAY

"I would congratulate and thank France for having the guts to go in there and do what we all should be doing to help Ukraine fight this illegal, immoral, inhumane war that Russia is persecuting the Ukrainian people with," Breedlove said.

RFI reported that French lawmakers had not been formally informed of the deployment, with authorities maintaining that parliamentary approval was unnecessary because the mission did not involve combat operations.

France has trained approximately 25,000 Ukrainian soldiers in France and Poland since 2023, according to Le Monde.

Macron raised the possibility of sending Western military instructors into Ukraine in 2024, prompting concerns among allies, including the United States and Germany, about a potential escalation with Moscow.

France has also helped lead efforts to establish a multinational force to support a potential postwar security arrangement for Ukraine.

Russia has repeatedly opposed the presence of Western troops in Ukraine, while Putin has characterized Western military assistance to Kyiv as evidence of a proxy conflict between Russia and NATO.

TRUMP PUSHED NATO TO SPEND BIG — NOW COMES THE HARDER QUESTION: CAN EUROPE ACTUALLY FIGHT?

The reports surfaced as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced fresh talks Monday with American and European representatives aimed at ending the war.

Zelenskyy said Ukrainian officials held online discussions with U.S. presidential envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, along with European representatives, about prospects for a negotiated settlement with Russia.

The Ukrainian leader also warned that intelligence indicated Russia was preparing major strikes against Ukrainian targets Monday evening, overnight and Tuesday.

Breedlove suggested that France's reported mission could now encourage other NATO members to further expand their support for Ukraine.

"I think that there are more than a few NATO nations that would love to be in there helping," he said.

"They're the ones that call themselves the Eastern Front, those nations that border Russia in various parts of the eastern flank of NATO."

"And so I'm sure there are other nations that want to do this, but they're looking for leadership to go do it," he said.

"It seems now that France may be stepping up to the task."

item.title: Boston Globe compares Dianna Russini to Bob Woodward amid Vrabel-sourcing scandal
item.description: The Boston Globe compares NFL reporter Dianna Russini to Bob Woodward over her closeness to Patriots coach Mike Vrabel, but the paper sees a difference.
item.content:encoded:
The Boston Globe argues that NFL reporter Dianna Russini might be best described as the modern-day Bob Woodward.

Last week, Russini returned to media after a seven-month hiatus following various outlets obtaining photos of her in a pool, at a bar, at a casino, and renting a private boat (while pregnant) with New England Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel.

Russini resigned from The Athletic in April amid an internal investigation into her failure to disclose her relationship with a source and subject, whether romantic or not. She now hosts a weekly podcast for offshore gambling company BetUS.

DIANNA RUSSINI'S CRINGE PODCAST DEBUT RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT THE VIABILITY OF HER COMEBACK

Despite the unusual circumstances, the Globe's Joan Vennochi drew parallels between Russini and Woodward, who also got too close to a source.

"There’s no compromising photo of Woodward in a hot tub with Richard Darman, the powerful official in two long-ago presidential administrations, as there was of Russini and New England Patriots coach Mike Vrabel while she was reporting on the NFL," Vennochi wrote.

"But in a piece in The New Yorker titled 'The Danger of Getting Too Close to a Source,' which is drawn from his new book, 'Secrets: A Reporter’s Memoir,' Woodward describes an intimate relationship with Darman that, figuratively speaking, put him in similar hot water.

In the article referenced, Woodward acknowledges that he "should have realized the danger" of his relationship with Darman but also that "the information flow and the time with Darman was so valuable."

The Globe article did, however, distinguish the two reporters in one way:

"[O]nce sex is involved, or speculated about, as it was with Russini and Vrabel (although neither has acknowledged it), such a relationship is automatically wrong for the journalist.

"But take the sex out of it — which no one ever can — and, as all journalists know, the same ethics questions arise. At what point does closeness not only cloud objectivity but also hamper the ability to tell the full truth if that truth hurts your source?," wrote Vennochi.

BOBBY BURACK: DIANNA RUSSINI WANTS SYMPATHY WITHOUT ACCOUNTABILITY IN MIKE VRABEL SCANDAL

Despite the bizarre comparison, the Globe misses the point: Woodward acknowledged the error in his judgment. Russini hasn't.

Russini looks worse today than she did when the first photo of her and Vrabel alone at an adults-only resort in Arizona leaked. She has taken no accountability. Instead, she has blamed the media and unnamed "lies" for her circumstances.

Last week, ahead of her return, Russini cast herself as a heroine for other women.

"I really hope that I can be someone other women see: you can pick yourself up, get back in there and not be afraid," Russini told People.

At the very least, Russini should do what Woodward and countless other journalists have done: admit she crossed boundaries with a source and vow to do better.

Instead, she maintains her innocence as if the rest of us are that gullible. Her arrogance continues to be her downfall.

If anything, Russini has positioned herself as the poster child for how not to handle getting too close to a source. She is hardly the sympathetic figure she depicts herself as.

The comparison to Woodward only makes her refusal to take accountability look worse.

item.title: NFL promoting that Raiders coaches and players spoke to Francisco Mendoza in Spanish is a virtue signal stunt
item.description: Las Vegas Raiders' Spanish-language communication with quarterback Fernando Mendoza felt forced, scripted and not organic.
item.content:encoded:
I considered writing this column in Spanish because I've covered the NFL for 36 years and, apparently, now that Fernando Mendoza is a starting quarterback, America's most popular professional sports league wants everyone to know it embraces Spanish.

What a time to be alive!

I was born in Cuba and embrace Spanish, too. It's my first language.

But I've been doing my job in English seemingly forever because I live in the United States and English is the language here. And an NFL locker room has had about as much to do with communicating in Spanish as it does in Swahili.

But since Mendoza is of Cuban descent (yeah, we're everywhere) and his parents are of Cuban descent, and his grandparents came from Cuba, someone at the NFL decided this an opportunity for some sort of outreach to Hispanics.

So when the Las Vegas Raiders had players and coaches speak some Spanish to Mendoza on Sunday during their game, the NFL saw this as a chance to pump itself as a global brand.

Did I mention Mendoza happened to be mic'd up to pick up teammate Aidan O'Connell tell him to "respira," which means breathe in Spanish? What a coincidence.

FERNANDO MENDOZA EMBRACES 'ONCE-IN-A-LIFETIME' CHANCE AS RAIDERS' QB1, CREDITS KIRK COUSINS' MENTORSHIP

The mic caught one Las Vegas coach throwing a random Spanish word here and there at Mendoza on the sideline.

And the league took those moments and did a look-at-us post on X to show that it's got some Spanish going on.

There is a phrase for this in my country: Virtue signaling.

THREE NFL TEAMS ROASTED FOR CELEBRATING INDIGENOUS PEOPLES' DAY ON COLUMBUS DAY, WHICH NO TEAM EVEN MENTIONED

It's not only unwelcome but opens up the NFL for mockery because it is not organic. It feels forced.

Why?

Firstly, Mendoza is American. Yes, his cultural origins cannot be denied. But he was born in this country and understandably speaks English much more fluently than he does Spanish – like many Hispanics his age living in the United States.

Secondly, is the NFL doing this for its quarterbacks of German descent? Or Italian? Or any other ethnicity?

Thirdly, the folks trying to somehow talk to Mendoza on the sideline in his non-native tongue weren't really speaking Spanish. They weren't stringing cogent sentences together. They were merely throwing out a Spanish word here and there.

It seemed forced.

At one point, a Raiders assistant coach told Mendoza, "Tu eres chingon."

The phrase is used by Mexicans and translates to 'You are awesome."

I think that's true because, although I speak Spanish fluently, I had to go look it up because I am not Mexican. And neither is Mendoza. And Spanish spoken in some countries, such as Mexico, is different from Spanish spoken in other countries, such as Cuba.

Breaking! People of Puerto Rican, Honduran, Mexican, Dominican or Venezuelan descent playing or coaching in the NFL don't all speak the same kind of Spanish. Some, like Minnesota Vikings defensive coordinator Brian Flores, aren't comfortable speaking Spanish at all.

So those players and coaches might look at someone telling them "Tu eres chingon" just like someone from Iowa or West Virginia might.

People in Texas speak differently than those in New York. Americans go to England and understand that our shared language is not identical.

So it is with Spanish.

That's why this gimmick post by the NFL actually shows how little the league actually understands Hispanics.

ZERO BS. JUST DAKICH. TAKE THE DON'T @ ME PODCAST ON THE ROAD. DOWNLOAD NOW!

Look, it may seem nice that the NFL tried to give Mendoza's ancestry a tip of the cap. But anyone doing their homework would know that the first Raiders quarterback with Hispanic roots was Tom Flores, who also happened to coach the team to two Super Bowl victories.

He never had any of his coaches or players speak to Jim Plunkett in Spanish even though, you know, Plunkett was also of Hispanic descent.

Then again, virtue signaling wasn't a thing in the NFL back then.

item.title: United Airlines says technology issue resolved after ‘widespread system outage’
item.description: United Airlines flights were stuck on tarmacs as pilots reported a companywide IT issue preventing takeoff data, days after the nationwide FAA ground stop.
item.content:encoded:
United Airlines said Monday it resolved a technology issue that delayed departing flights, marking another disruption for travelers just days after a nationwide FAA ground stop.

"We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures. While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights," United Media Relations told Fox News Digital.

"There is no indication that this was a cybersecurity-related issue," the airline added.

Earlier Monday, passengers reported being unable to take off, with one saying their flight was returning to the gate because the crew could not obtain performance data needed for departure.

FORMER TOP FAA OFFICIAL WARNS OF 48-HOUR RECOVERY AFTER AGING TECH 'OVERWHELMED' AHEAD OF GROUND STOP

United initially acknowledged a widespread outage in a response to a passenger on X.

"We're aware of the widespread system outage, and our teams are working hard to get things back up and running as soon as possible," United’s official X account wrote in response to a passenger.

The airline apologized and urged travelers to monitor their flight status through the United app or its website. Its response did not identify the cause or provide an estimated restoration time.

One passenger reported being stuck on the tarmac, saying crews could not clear planes for takeoff because they could not connect to a weight system.

Another social media user said their flight was returning to the gate after the pilot announced a company wide IT issue that left the crew "unable to get performance data for takeoff."

"Pilot just announced ALL of United Airlines has a company wide IT issue," the user wrote. "We’re going back to the gate."

Another passenger reported a similar announcement while waiting for departure.

"Waiting to take off, on the runway, and the pilot just said we can’t take off because United is experiencing a system-wide computer outage," the user wrote.

AMERICA HITS A TECH WALL AS OUTAGES CRIPPLE EMAIL, GROUND FLIGHTS AND DISRUPT MAJOR BANKS

The X account @theATCapp also posted that it was receiving reports of a systemwide IT outage affecting the airline.

United’s response acknowledged a widespread outage but did not confirm the passengers’ descriptions of the affected systems. The number of flights and airports affected was not immediately clear.

Flight-tracking service Flightradar24 reported that United’s mainline departures were beginning to resume.

"We are seeing mainline departures resuming in the last few minutes," the service posted on X.

At Los Angeles International Airport, Fox News correspondent Max Gorden spoke with several passengers at the United counter who were able to check in for their flights. However, an agent showed Gorden her United mobile device, which appeared to be experiencing technical problems.

The outage comes after a telecommunications failure prompted the Federal Aviation Administration to issue a nationwide ground stop Friday, Nov. 13. The restriction was later lifted, but airlines faced lingering delays and cancellations as they worked to restore their schedules.

Following Friday’s ground stop, United CEO Scott Kirby praised the FAA’s decision to halt flights and thanked employees and customers for their patience. He also called for better technology and full staffing to help prevent future outages.

Kirby said he had spoken directly with Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy, FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford and aviation leaders from both parties in Congress about the impact on United’s passengers and employees.

"This moment must be a call to action," Kirby said in a statement shared with Fox News Digital.

"It is critical for safety, our passengers, and our economy that we fix our nation’s Air Traffic Control system now."

Kirby said lawmakers from both parties were committed to modernizing the system while holding the FAA accountable.

There was no immediate confirmation that United’s outage Monday was connected to Friday’s FAA disruption.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

item.title: JD Vance says he and Trump still 'don't know' whether Alice Huang was a Chinese spy
item.description: JD Vance says intelligence on whether Alice Huang spied for China points in different directions, as Nvidia faces national security scrutiny over chips.
item.content:encoded:
Vice President JD Vance said he and President Donald Trump are still unsure about whether Alice Huang, the Chinese businesswoman at the center of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's extramarital affairs, was working as a Chinese spy, even after reviewing intelligence.

"I think what the president is just pointing at is there is a lack of clarity about it. I don't know. And he doesn't know whether this woman was a spy or not," Vance told host Laura Ingraham.

The vice president discussed the controversy surrounding Nvidia, as well as Friday’s nationwide ground stop, during an interview on "The Ingraham Angle" set to air Monday at 7 p.m. ET.

FOREIGN SPY ‘HONEYTRAPS’ TARGETING AMERICA’S TECH ELITE SPARK ALARM AMID NVIDIA CEO SCANDAL

TUNE IN TO WATCH VICE PRESIDENT VANCE'S INTERVIEW ON ‘THE INGRAHAM ANGLE AT 7PM ET ON FOX NEWS!

U.S. officials suspect Alice Huang was recruited by China to influence Nvidia to make its advanced chips more available to Beijing, according to the New York Times. The Chinese businesswoman became a regular presence in Jensen Huang’s professional circle, frequently accompanying him to corporate events and dinners.

Vance told Fox News that the intelligence he viewed on the investigation was not sufficient enough for him and the president to conclude that Alice Huang was spying on behalf of China, arguing that intel can sometimes be conflicting.

CHINA’S GREAT AI CHIP LOOPHOLE: HOW AMERICAN ESPIONAGE STOPPED CHINA — THIS TIME

"The reason is because this intelligence always points in different directions," Vance said. "The thing I've learned about intelligence, Laura, I think Henry Kissinger once said that you think you're really smart by reading all the intelligence, and then you realize that because the intelligence disagrees with itself."

The espionage allegations, as well as Jensen Huang’s admission to engaging in extramarital affairs, rocked the stock market and raised national security concerns.

A SPY TOOK OUT NVIDIA’S CEO. HERE’S HOW AMERICA STILL WINS THE AI RACE

Many believe the Chinese businesswoman could have been gathering intelligence on one of America’s most highly valued technology companies for China.

Nvidia has said, however, Huang’s meetings with Alice Huang were not unusual, adding that he meets with thousands of executives each year.

Vance said the fact of whether Alice Huang was spying for China or not is largely insignificant in the broader scandal. The vice president said strengthening America's domestic industrial base and safeguarding critical technology takes precedence.

MASSIVE AI BOOM PUTS ONE OF AMERICA’S OLDEST MANUFACTURERS ON PATH TO DOUBLE IN SIZE, CEO SAYS

"That actually is not the main issue. The main issue is we need to industrialize the country and protect our critical technology and our critical infrastructure," he said. "And the only way to do that is to build more of it in the United States of America and prevent it from falling into the wrong hands."

China has rejected allegations of Alice Huang being a spy and the Justice Department has not determined whether she was providing Beijing with intelligence.

item.title: Devin Hester says chasing rabbits through Florida sugarcane fields helped build NFL speed
item.description: Devin Hester says chasing rabbits through sugarcane fields in the Glades helped shape his legendary speed, with catches earning up to $60 on weekends.
item.content:encoded:
Devin Hester made a Hall of Fame career out of being faster than just about everyone else on the football field. And apparently, growing up in South Florida came with some pretty unconventional speed training.

In a recent interview with Whistle, the legendary Chicago Bears return specialist was asked what makes football players from Florida different. His answer? Year-round football, plenty of time playing outside and, believe it or not, chasing rabbits.

"I'm from West Palm, and so West Palm out in the Glades area, they ran in the Muck where they chase the rabbits," Hester said. "They get paid for catching rabbits."

CLICK HERE FOR MORE COVERAGE FROM OUTKICK OUTDOORS

Yes, actual rabbits. And it wasn't just a game.

"You had family members that ate rabbits. So like, you catch a rabbit, kill them. You catch about three rabbits. That's about $60," Hester explained.

When the interviewer asked what he meant by running in the Muck, Hester clarified that he was talking about sugarcane fields.

"That's how you made your money on the weekends," he said.

SIGN UP FOR THE DAILY OUTKICK NEWSLETTER

Hester added that while he never ate the rabbits himself, he had aunts, uncles and grandfathers who did.

And if this all sounds a little strange, there's actually quite a bit of history behind it.

In the agricultural communities surrounding Lake Okeechobee — particularly Belle Glade and Pahokee — chasing rabbits through sugarcane fields has been a tradition for generations. The region is nicknamed "the Muck" for its dark, fertile soil.

During sugarcane harvests, farmers traditionally burned the fields to clear away excess vegetation, sending rabbits running out of the cane. Locals would chase them down, sometimes catching them by hand. Some rabbits were eaten, while others were sold for extra money.

A 2013 Washington Post story about former Maryland cornerback Will Likely detailed the practice, describing rabbit chasing as a way of life in the Muck rather than simply a childhood pastime.

The tradition was also featured in the 2023 PBS documentary "Outta the Muck," which explores the history, culture and football legacy of Pahokee.

And Hester certainly isn't the only NFL player with a connection to rabbit chasing.

Former Cleveland Browns wide receiver and return specialist Travis Benjamin, who grew up in Belle Glade, once credited the activity for his agility.

PANTHERS' XAVIER LEGETTE GRATEFUL FOR TEAMMATES, INCLUDING QB BRYCE YOUNG, EXPERIENCING HIS COUNTRY LIFESTYLE

"I really do think chasing rabbits helped me develop agility," Benjamin told the Browns' official website in 2014. "Sometimes when I watch my punt returns on film, it reminds me of being a kid with the rabbits."

Benjamin said he caught hundreds of rabbits growing up, including 15 during his first outing when he was just 12 years old. His speed eventually earned him the nickname "The Rabbit" from his Browns teammates.

And Hester, of course, went on to become one of the most dangerous return men in NFL history. The four-time Pro Bowler and three-time first-team All-Pro retired with an NFL-record 20 combined return touchdowns and became the first player inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame primarily as a return specialist.
